newsitem.title: UK: Bank shares motor ahead in buoyant London market.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares motor ahead in buoyant London market.

text.p: Banks were Tuesday's star performers on the London Stock Exchange on Tuesday with a strong overnight performance of HSBC shares in Hong Kong setting the tone and putting the whole sector in the limelight again.
A weighty 100-page review on the banking industry here by brokers Dresdner Kleinwort Benson also helped spark solid buying interest, dealers said.
HSBC Holdings Plc powered ahead to close at a 12-month high as it advanced 84-1/2 pence to 2,085 with Kleinwort upping its target price by 300 pence to 2400 pence.
Dealers said the upgrade was mainly based on valuation ground, dealers said, while Kleinwort analysts declined to comment.

Kleinwort was said to have also upgraded Standard Chartered Plc, up 26-1/2 pence to 1,000p and Barclays Plc, which gained 18 pence to 1,252p. Both banks were raised to "add" from "hold", dealers said.
One trader believed the latest rally in banking shares reflected a lack of fresh ideas among bullish investors.

"With only a few exceptions, people feel confident in the same sectors that have been outperforming the market for months now," he said, as the London market closed at a new all-time high for the second day in a row.
The FTSE 100 Index finished 41.9 points higher at 4,899.3.

"We've been led by the pharmaceuticals and financial sectors and until we see some improvement in manufacturing and engineering, people are going to stick with the visible earners," this dealer added.
But shares in Halifax Plc and Alliance & Leicester Plc lagged as investors shunned the newly de-mutualised building societies because of stretched valuations, dealers and analysts said.
"Valuations are too high, and mortgage banking growth is slowing. There's a lot of froth in this market," said one analyst.
A disappointing performance by Woolwich Plc, floated on July 7, also has taken some of the lustre out the former building societies, another analyst added.
Shares in Halifax retreated two pence to 754-1/2. Shares in A&L firmed 1-/2 pence to 621-1/2 while Woolwich lost four pence to close at 299.
